title: Les aventures du philosophe inconnu, en la recherche & en l'invention de la pierre philosophale
shelf_note: A 1646 French alchemical-devotional work (Belin); the page is 17th-century French print with long s and u/v. No tradition or collection is given to check against, and nothing on the page contradicts the record.
structure_note: Scan page 162 carries printed p. 140, a 22-leaf offset that is plausible for front matter. Backsteps (7) and repeats (8) among 221 printed numbers more likely come from misread numerals than from a splice, but one page cannot confirm that. The structure count says 0 pages translated, while the field says 236 and this page has a translation, so the count is stale or wrong (E2).

ocr_errors.problem: running head silently normalised u→v, while the body keeps the u/v spelling ("trouue", "deuoir")

tr_errors.english: The Lord takes pleasure in going out onto the field
tr_errors.problem: "Seigneur" here means a nobleman going out to duel, not God. In a passage about God, "The Lord" with a capital reads as God; only the duel note and the context let the reader recover the meaning

book_verdict: The page is the right leaf and its transcription is almost exact; the translation is faithful apart from rendering a duelling "Seigneur" as "The Lord". The notes are sound. Leaked arrow-and-bold markup in the running head is the defect a reader sees on sight.
